Package sootup.core.typehierarchy

Class ViewTypeHierarchy

java.lang.Object
sootup.core.typehierarchy.ViewTypeHierarchy
All Implemented Interfaces:
MutableTypeHierarchy, TypeHierarchy
public class ViewTypeHierarchy extends Object implements MutableTypeHierarchy
Stores class relations as dense integer ids plus two encodings tailored to the two different shapes the Java type hierarchy actually has:
  • class-extends-class is single inheritance, i.e. a forest. Each class gets a contiguous [rangeStart, rangeEnd) position range into a single L2R pre-order DFS array (ViewTypeHierarchy.RawAdjacency/ViewTypeHierarchy.TypeHierarchyEncoding.classHierarchyOrder), so "is B a subtype of A" is an O(1) range-containment test and "all subtypes of A" is an O(k) array slice - no traversal needed. This mirrors phasar's DIBasedTypeHierarchy encoding for (single-inheritance) C++ class hierarchies.
  • interface-extends-interface and class-implements-interface form a general DAG (multiple supertypes), which a single contiguous range cannot encode. Interfaces get their own dense sub-numbering and a bitset per interface holding all transitively extended interfaces (self-inclusive), computed once via bottom-up DP over the interface DAG. Subtype tests against an interface are then O(1) bit tests instead of a graph walk.

Documentation about how to use it is available here.

Author:
Christian Brüggemann

  • Method Details

    • getModificationCount

      public long getModificationCount()
      Description copied from interface: TypeHierarchy
      Returns a counter that increases every time the hierarchy's structure is mutated (e.g. via MutableTypeHierarchy.addType(sootup.core.model.SootClass), including mutations triggered internally by lazy resolution of previously-unseen types). Callers that build their own caches derived from hierarchy queries (e.g. call graph algorithms caching resolved dispatch targets) can compare this value across calls to detect staleness without needing to be notified of every individual mutation.
      Specified by:
      getModificationCount in interface TypeHierarchy

    • implementersOf

      public @NonNull Stream<ClassType> implementersOf(@NonNull ClassType interfaceType)
      Description copied from interface: TypeHierarchy
      Returns all classes that implement the specified interface. This is transitive: If class A extends B and B implements interface, then this method will return both A and B as implementers of interfaceType.

      This includes interfaces extending interfaceType as they may contain default implementations of methods.

      Specified by:
      implementersOf in interface TypeHierarchy

    • subtypeClassesOf

      public @NonNull Stream<? extends SootClass> subtypeClassesOf(@NonNull ClassType type)
      Description copied from interface: TypeHierarchy
      Equivalent to resolving every element of TypeHierarchy.subtypesOf(ClassType) to its SootClass via the underlying View, i.e. subtypesOf(type).flatMap(ct -> view.getClass(ct).stream()) - a subtype the View cannot resolve on its own (e.g. one added via MutableTypeHierarchy.addType(sootup.core.model.SootClass) with a class instance the view doesn't know about) is silently excluded, same as that composition would produce. Implementations are expected to cache this resolution (invalidated the same way as TypeHierarchy.subtypesOf(ClassType)), since callers such as call graph algorithms query the same declaring type repeatedly across many call sites.
      Specified by:
      subtypeClassesOf in interface TypeHierarchy

    • implementedInterfacesOf

      public @NonNull Stream<ClassType> implementedInterfacesOf(@NonNull ClassType type)
      Description copied from interface: TypeHierarchy
      Returns the interfaces implemented by type if it is a class or extended by type if it is an interface. This includes interfaces implemented by superclasses and also covers the case where classType directly or indirectly implements an interface I1 that extends another interface I2 . I2 will be considered an implemented interface of classType.
